title: The UI guide — exact wording for three roles

steps.intro: Yes approves only the exact quoted rule; No asks for a revision; Don't know defers. No screen changes follow automatically.

steps.path: Settings, About and Development, Project details, Marketplace details, Tags & note, Resume Session
steps.headline: Should this be the guide’s rule for outer popup titles?
steps.today: You chose and accepted 16px medium titles on Settings and the reviewed titled popups. Full-page headings, list names and item labels have different jobs.
steps.problem: A blanket 'all titles match' rule would also enlarge file names, section labels and menu rows, or crowd Back and Close on narrow screens.
steps.proposal: Exact rule: “Use a 16px medium-weight title for the outer header of Settings and titled popups. Page headings, section labels, row labels, file and entry names, and buttons have their own hierarchy; don't resize them just to match popup titles. Leave room for Back, Close, and long titles.”
steps.risk: This would guide future titled popups. It does not change untitled menus or approve a universal text size.

steps.path: Settings and the separately accepted titled popup shells
steps.headline: Should this be the guide’s rule for a popup header above scrolling content?
steps.today: Settings, shared dialogs, Project and Marketplace details, the file viewer, Tags & note, and Resume's list side have reviewed header/body treatments. The wide Assistant settings rail scrolls differently.
steps.problem: A painted fade can clash with a tapered line on wallpaper themes. But making every internal separator fade would erase useful structure.
steps.proposal: Exact rule: “On the reviewed fixed-header, separately scrolling Settings and titled-popup shells, draw a 1px header line inset 16px per side and tapered over the first and last 8% of its span. Where more body content is hidden, fade the content at that edge over 42px, softening the outer 4%; otherwise show no fade. Do not paint a panel-colored strip. Structural row borders, Markdown rules, metadata boundaries, internal separators, untitled dialogs and the wide Assistant settings rail are separate roles; review new custom shells before using this recipe.”
steps.risk: Only reviewed header/body shells, not every titled popup, divider or scrolling list. A new custom shell gets its own visual check.

steps.intro: Yes approves both distinct sentences below; No with a note revises either one. This is wording only, not a Session Files production edit.

steps.path: A conversation → Files; a project → Files
steps.headline: Should this be the guide’s rule for these two file views?
steps.today: Session Files still shows flat rows; you chose compact inset cards in its visual comparison. Project Files already offers both a preview grid and a dense list; phone download cards serve another task.
steps.problem: Copying the Project grid into Session Files would invent previews. Forcing every file view into cards would lose a useful dense list and obscure the phone's different download action.
steps.proposal: Exact rule: “In Session Files, use compact inset cards for files without previews: put the filename first, then a short status and date, with a quiet outline; do not invent a thumbnail. In Project Files, keep both the preview grid and dense list, choosing by task and available preview. Phone download cards and other file surfaces may use their own treatment.”
steps.risk: Filename legibility and touch/keyboard access to Remove remain functional requirements, not aesthetic choices. No universal file-card rule is proposed.
